name: SpaceX
day_summary: Sunday — US equity markets closed for a third consecutive day (Juneteenth June 19 + Saturday June 20 + Sunday June 21). No SPCX trading. SPCX remains in STEP_ASIDE mode at the last confirmed close of $174.90 (June 18). The investment-grade credit ratings from all three major agencies (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+, all stable outlook) have now been unpriced for 72+ hours — June 22 (Monday) is the first and only pricing opportunity. OVERNIGHT UPDATE: MSCI assigned SpaceX an ESG rating of CCC (lowest on the scale), citing governance and sustainability concerns — does NOT affect IG credit standing but adds a reputational overlay that institutional ESG-mandated funds must weigh; long-term framework unchanged. MACRO CAUTION: Prediction market for June 22 SPX open (Lines.com) shows 56% probability of opening DOWN (vs morning's SPX futures +0.74%); macro setup into Monday is less unambiguously constructive than earlier in the day. BTC Day 1 stop re-triggered (June 21 UTC close $63,313 < $63,500) — reduces the 'risk-on tailwind' score for SPCX's gap-up scenario. Framework unchanged: two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume required for re-entry. Watch June 22 open level carefully — scenario framework from the morning remains the guide.

No re-entry before two consecutive daily closes above $185 on above-average volume. June 22 scenarios: (1) SPCX gaps to or above $185 on IG momentum + SPX futures +0.74% → watch for the CLOSE above $185 (need first of two consecutive closes); (2) SPCX opens $175–$185 with strong volume (>150M shares) → begin 3–5 session stabilization watch, stop for new entry at $165; (3) SPCX opens at or above $190 → IG ratings fully priced in one session; hold for second consecutive close above $185 before re-entry; (4) SPCX opens below $165 → correction extending; June 22 weekly options expiry now at July frame; July $175 put (at ~52% IV) is the hedge vehicle for any new long position established above $185.

positioning.iv_note: IV stabilized at ~52% after the June 18 spike to ~58–60%. June 20 weekly expiry clearing removes the short-dated options structure that was driving highest IV. July options at ~52% IV are the reference vehicle for any re-entry. The IG rating development is structurally IV-reducing: IG status reduces the perceived default tail and expands the institutional ownership base toward more stable holders. If SPCX gaps up materially on June 22 (IG rating pricing), IV could initially spike on the event before compressing as the institutional ownership quality improves. A July $175 put would cost approximately $11–13 at current IV as a re-entry hedge.
positioning.short_interest: P/C at 1.12 (from 1.15 June 20, 1.18 June 19, 1.20 peak June 18). Borrow availability continuing to normalize post-IPO Day 10+. The remaining short thesis rests on valuation (84x revenue) and September 2 earnings uncertainty, not credit quality.

outlook.short_term: The June 22 open is the week's defining moment for SPCX. Three forces converge simultaneously: (1) 72+ hours of unpriced IG ratings from all three major agencies; (2) SPX futures +0.74% suggesting a constructive broad-market open; (3) DXY at ~100.23 (most constructive macro for the 84x multiple since the stop trigger). If SPCX gaps to $185+ on June 22 open on strong volume, the re-entry framework activates: watch for the first CLOSE above $185 (need two consecutive before re-entry). The most important principle: one gap-up session above $185 is not re-entry — two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume is the defined standard. The step-aside framework is not a permanent exit; it's a disciplined re-entry filter.
outlook.long_term: Generational franchise, now with triple-IG validation. Moody's Baa1 + Fitch BBB+ + S&P BBB — independently assessed within days of the IPO — are permanent franchise-quality anchors that cannot be unpriced. Starlink at 5M+ subscribers growing ~40% annually, Starship cost-to-orbit structural economics, Starshield national-security base load, and Cursor AI software layer (not in IG franchise assessment) are all intact. The September 2 first earnings print is the event that converts the IG-validated franchise into disclosed financials. The December 9 lock-up expiry (180-day) is the first major float expansion. Both events create catalysts for re-rating in either direction — IG ratings are the floor; September 2 earnings is the ceiling catalyst.

bull_case: IG ratings (S&P BBB, Moody's Baa1, Fitch BBB+) unpriced for 72+ hours — the single most significant fundamental development since the IPO; Moody's Baa1 above Tesla's Baa3 is a legitimacy signal that SpaceX franchise quality exceeds the most recognized IG industrial-tech precedent; June 22 is the one-time pricing event; SPX futures +0.74% + DXY improving = optimal conditions for a IG-gap toward $185.

June 20 weekly options expiry CLEARED + July IV at ~52% (down from June 18 spike of 58-60%) — clean options slate, no residual gamma headwind; if SPCX gaps to $185 on June 22 open, July OI re-anchors at the new price range; the combination of IG news + clean options slate is a structural clearing event for the post-stop technical overhang.

Analyst consensus: 6 buy / 1 sell with average PT $187.80 — six of seven analysts have buy ratings ABOVE $174.90; IG ratings provide the fundamental validation needed for analysts to raise PTs to $200+; if two or three analysts raise PTs to $200+ citing IG-adjusted cost-of-capital models before June 23, institutional accumulation restarts even without a re-entry confirmation.

SpaceX Cursor AI acquisition ($60B stock, 1M+ developer users) is not included in the IG rating assessments — IG ratings are based only on Starlink + Starship + Starshield disclosed cash flows; Cursor AI represents asymmetric upside that the rating agencies have not factored; September 2 first earnings will disclose Cursor revenue, providing the first 'upside not in the model' catalyst.
bear_case: $185 stop triggered at $174.90 — the framework's own risk management mandated exit; IG ratings arrived simultaneously with the stock declining (the market's vote on valuation preceded the rating agencies' vote on credit quality); credit market endorsement does not automatically translate to equity market reversal, especially when the valuation (84x revenue) remains unchanged.

84x revenue multiple at $174.90 — IG ratings lower the cost of capital but do not lower the revenue multiple; at September 2 earnings, SPCX needs to show Starlink subs growing >40% annually, Starship generating recurring launch revenue, and Cursor AI delivering initial software revenue — all to justify a $2.4T market cap; the 74-day wait until September 2 is a 74-day window of fundamental uncertainty during which the only anchor is franchise quality (not disclosed financials).

MSCI passive bid decelerating — Day 11+ post-IPO means the systematic MSCI rebalancing buying window is largely exhausted; the volume needed to re-establish $185 as support (>150M shares average) requires institutional buying to replace the passive mechanical bid; IG ratings help but may not fully offset the passive bid decline.

Jim Chanos valuation thesis intact — 84x revenue with net losses remains the most direct fundamental bear case; IG ratings validate cash flow durability but the stock is not being valued on cash flows at $2.4T; December 9 lock-up expiry creates a known supply-side overhang that limits the upside re-rating until Chanos-style value investors can see the first earnings report.
